columns.label: Day
columns.meaning: Synthetic sequential day number from 1 to 28.

columns.label: Athlete
columns.meaning: One invented outfielder throughout; no club or personal information.

columns.label: Phase
columns.meaning: Days 1–14 are the predefined reference window. Days 15–28 are monitoring; do not move the baseline after viewing results.

columns.label: CMJ height
columns.meaning: Mean of 3 valid force-plate CMJs using impulse-momentum height. Hands on hips except documented day 8 deviation. Blank means no measurement.

columns.label: Reported sleep
columns.meaning: Athlete-reported previous-night sleep duration. Contextual information, not an objective recovery measure.

columns.label: Previous game
columns.meaning: Innings played on the preceding calendar date; it is not a complete measure of running or training exposure.

columns.label: Previous 24 h travel
columns.meaning: Recorded travel within the 24 hours before testing. Day 25 travel occurs after testing and therefore appears in day 26’s field.

columns.label: Comparable protocol
columns.meaning: False marks the verified arm-swing deviation on day 8; true means no recorded protocol deviation, not proof of zero measurement error.

columns.label: Context note
columns.meaning: Source notes to support exclusion, temporal interpretation and follow-up. No symptom report is not equivalent to medical clearance.

cleaningRules: Keep all 28 raw rows. Do not overwrite day 8 or day 11.
Baseline = days 1–14, protocol_ok true and cmj_cm recorded. Exclude day 8 for verified protocol change and day 11 for a missing measurement; n = 12.
Use the sample SD of the eligible baseline observations. This is descriptive baseline variability, not an established SEM.
Current = day 28. Last-three-day mean = comparable observations on days 26, 27 and 28; state this exact window.
Review rule for this exercise: 2 consecutive comparable recorded days more than 1.5 cm below the fixed baseline mean. Missing or noncomparable days break the sequence.
Preserve time order: day 25’s late travel occurs after its morning jump and appears as prior-24-hour travel on day 26.
Do not interpolate missing values, refit the baseline after looking at the monitoring period, or label lower jump height as a quantified fatigue or injury state.
provenance: Entirely synthetic teaching data authored for this hub. Athlete IDs, dates, values, logs and scenarios are invented; no club or patient records were used. Values are for analysis practice, not validated injury-risk, readiness or clearance thresholds.
